reuseNote: All exemplars researched fresh in this run. Not recorded (pages blocked or search budget exhausted): OpenResearch $1,000/month study details, Colorado pay-range posting study, Gravity Payments, Alaska dividend. Repair run copied from 20261019-140024.

stockton-seed.name: Stockton Economic Empowerment Demonstration (SEED)
stockton-seed.outcome: 125 residents got $500 a month; full-time work rose from 28% to 40% in year one vs. smaller gain in control group
stockton-seed.limits: 125 people, funded by philanthropies (primarily the Economic Security Project), first-year results; people without permanent addresses excluded; pandemic overlapped later period; control group full-time work rose from 32% to 37%.
stockton-seed.locator: "increased their rate of full-time employment from 28% in February 2019"

ct-baby-bonds.name: Connecticut Baby Bonds
ct-baby-bonds.outcome: $3,200 invested for each baby born on the state's Medicaid program (HUSKY); usable from 18 for school, training, a home, a business or retirement in Connecticut
ct-baby-bonds.limits: Payouts start years from now, so no outcome data yet; start year from background knowledge (page confirms a July start); funding totals differ between reports.
ct-baby-bonds.locator: "$3,200 will be invested in the child's name"

ma-millionaires-tax.name: Massachusetts 4% surtax on household income above about $1.1 million
ma-millionaires-tax.outcome: Adopted after a 2022 push; raised more than $3.38 billion between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (fiscal 2026); meant only for education and transportation, such as universal free school meals, free community college and free regional transit buses
ma-millionaires-tax.limits: Revenue figures do not settle whether some high earners left; the WBUR piece reports the supporters' coalition view on that point; the article does not give the date the tax took effect.

irs-eitc-unclaimed.name: IRS estimate of unclaimed Earned Income Tax Credit
irs-eitc-unclaimed.outcome: About one in five eligible taxpayers don't claim the EITC; average credit about $2,541 (tax year 2022); IRS EITC Assistant checks eligibility
irs-eitc-unclaimed.limits: Archived 2024 release; amounts and rules change each tax year.
irs-eitc-unclaimed.locator: "about one in five of EITC eligible taxpayers don't claim this valuable credit"

irs-vita.name: IRS Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) and AARP Tax-Aide
irs-vita.outcome: Free tax preparation for people who generally make about $70,244 or less; locator tool and phone line
irs-vita.limits: Sites set their own limits and hours; mostly seasonal (January to April).
irs-vita.locator: "People who generally make about $ 70,244 or less"

ctc-2021-expiry.name: Expanded federal Child Tax Credit, 2021
ctc-2021-expiry.outcome: Supplemental child poverty rate rose from 5.2% in 2021 to 12.4% in 2022 after the expansion expired
ctc-2021-expiry.limits: Secondary news report of Census data; other pandemic aid also ended in 2022; effects on work are debated.
ctc-2021-expiry.locator: "more than doubled, from 5.2% in 2021 to 12.4% in 2022"

ca-fast-food-council.name: California Fast Food Council and $20 minimum wage
ca-fast-food-council.outcome: $20 minimum starting April 1, 2024, for fast food restaurants in California that belong to chains with at least 60 locations nationwide (some bakeries excluded); council can raise it up to 3.5% a year
ca-fast-food-council.limits: Deal struck between unions and industry partly to avoid a ballot fight; one industry, one state.
ca-fast-food-council.locator: "power to increase that minimum wage each year by up to 3.5%"

ca-fast-food-berkeley.name: UC Berkeley study of California's $20 fast food wage
ca-fast-food-berkeley.outcome: Hourly pay up about 18% on average; one-time price rise of about 3.7%; employment not adversely affected
ca-fast-food-berkeley.limits: Contested: critics cite seasonally adjusted data showing about 2,200 lost jobs; an industry-funded analysis reported larger losses.
ca-fast-food-berkeley.locator: "on a one-time basis only, by about 3.7%"

richer-sounds-eot.name: Richer Sounds employee ownership trust
richer-sounds-eot.outcome: Founder Julian Richer handed a 60% stake in the entertainment retailer, which has 53 stores across the UK, to a trust for staff; 522 employees got £1,000 per year of service, about £8,000 on average
richer-sounds-eot.limits: One founder's choice; UK trust tax rules differ from US options such as employee stock ownership plans.

preston-cwb.name: Preston community wealth building
preston-cwb.outcome: Share of six anchor institutions' spending in Preston rose from 5% (2012/13) to 19% (2016/17)
preston-cwb.limits: Written by someone involved in the project; total spending fell over the period; questions about procurement rules and effects on other areas.

boomer-succession.name: Project Equity estimate of baby boomer–owned businesses
boomer-succession.outcome: Project Equity, an Oakland, California-based nonprofit, says baby boomers own 2.34 million businesses employing 24.7 million people; a separate estimate says 80 percent of these businesses lack a plan for what comes next
boomer-succession.limits: 2017 article citing older Census data; Project Equity advocates employee ownership; the 80 percent figure is attributed to a University of Wisconsin source.
boomer-succession.locator: "baby boomers own 2.34 million businesses, employ 24.7 million people"

norway-wealth-tax.name: Norway wealth tax rise and departures
norway-wealth-tax.outcome: Top wealth tax rate set at 1.1%; at least 30 billionaires and millionaires moved abroad in 2022, more than the previous 13 years combined
norway-wealth-tax.limits: Counts of departures vary by source; revenue effects disputed; Norway taxes wealth, not just income.
norway-wealth-tax.locator: "greater than in the previous 13 years combined"

myfriendben.name: MyFriendBen benefits screener
myfriendben.outcome: Helped over 55,000 Colorado households apply for $33 million in benefits within two years
myfriendben.limits: Self-reported by its founding funder; Colorado programs only.

champlain-housing-trust.name: Champlain Housing Trust
champlain-housing-trust.outcome: The trust, in Vermont, keeps the land and sells only the home, so the land cost is not in the price; a Davis and Stokes evaluation found sellers gained about $12,000 on resale while homes stayed affordable; $2.1 million of subsidies retained
champlain-housing-trust.limits: Resale equity is capped, so owners build less wealth than in a rising open market; founding year from background knowledge.
champlain-housing-trust.locator: "the net equity gain to a homeowner on resale was $12,000"

right-to-discuss-pay.name: US Labor Department worker rights: discussing wages
right-to-discuss-pay.outcome: Lists openly talking with coworkers about wages, benefits and conditions as a protected right
right-to-discuss-pay.limits: Covers most private-sector employees; supervisors and some others are generally excluded.
right-to-discuss-pay.locator: "openly talking with one or more coworkers about your wages"

mondragon.name: Mondragon cooperatives pay cap
mondragon.outcome: Pay gap between highest and lowest paid capped at 6 to 1; nearly 70,000 member-owners
mondragon.limits: Not all workers are members; international subsidiaries are not co-ops; Fagor went bankrupt after 2008.

acs-gini.name: Census American Community Survey Gini index (table B19083)
acs-gini.outcome: County Gini 0.435 vs. California 0.485 and US 0.483 (2024 1-year estimates)
acs-gini.limits: 1-year estimates cover only larger counties; Gini is one summary number and hides wealth gaps.
acs-gini.locator: "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey, 1-Year Estimates (Table B19083)"

maf-lending-circles.name: Mission Asset Fund lending circles
maf-lending-circles.outcome: Members with no score or a poor score were almost twice as likely to gain 20 points as a comparison group
maf-lending-circles.limits: Quasi-experimental study of one neighborhood, 2011–2013; no effect for people starting above 620.

nceo-esops.name: NCEO count of US employee stock ownership plans
nceo-esops.outcome: 6,609 ESOPs at about 6,400 companies (6,411), 15.1 million participants; ESOPs paid out over $166 billion to participants in 2023
nceo-esops.limits: Advocacy research group; plan quality and payouts vary widely.

usa-gov-officials.name: USA.gov elected officials directory
usa-gov-officials.outcome: Names and contact information for federal, state and local representatives
usa-gov-officials.limits: Directory only; separate lookups by level of government.
usa-gov-officials.locator: "people who represent you on the federal, state, and local levels"

pay-transparency-laws.name: US state pay transparency laws
pay-transparency-laws.outcome: New York enacted a pay transparency law in 2023 requiring employers to publicly disclose job salary ranges; other states with compensation transparency laws as of 2023 include California, Connecticut, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Nevada, Rhode Island and Washington
pay-transparency-laws.limits: Encyclopedia summary; laws differ by state; no effect on pay gaps is measured on this page.
pay-transparency-laws.locator: "The law requires employers to publicly disclose job salary ranges."
